text:
maria: quick heads-up — i've sketched a proposal to pull the latency-sensitive hot path out of request-router into a minimal, single-purpose service. goal: reduce p99 on short-turnaround requests (seq len < 128) without touching the broader router code.
kevin: curious — what does the surface look like? RPC overhead might hurt small requests.
maria: agreed. contract is intentionally tiny: pre-validated proto + preference hints -> token-stream chunks or a short-circuit response. fallback to router if the hot service is unavailable. proto sketch below.
aj: can you paste the proto? also thinking: is a library (in-process) an option? avoids RPC but complicates deploy and memory pressure per worker.
maria: proto:
```
service HotPathService {
  rpc Generate(HotRequest) returns (stream TokenChunk) {}
}
message HotRequest { string trace_id = 1; bytes pretokenized_prompt = 2; int32 max_tokens = 3; map<string,string> hints = 4; }
message TokenChunk { repeated int32 token_ids = 1; bool done = 2; }
```
sophia: +1 on keeping it minimal. instrumentation needs: per-request path tag, tokens_out, latency_ms, and a span that correlates to the parent request. we also need a metric for fallback rate (hotpath->router).
ryan: rollout plan thoughts: feature-flagged by route + tenant. start with 1% traffic in canary region, compare p50/p95/p99, error budget burn, and cost per token. we should also keep end-to-end latency histograms (client-observed) to catch added network hop regressions.
kevin: about library vs service: if we ship as a sidecar (co-located process) we get low-latency RPC (unix socket) and independent deploys. that seems like a middle ground.
aj: sidecar + versioned unix-socket API would be attractive. also ask: how do we handle warm KV cache? hotpath needs to access KV cache; duplicating cache will complicate coherency.
maria: plan is to treat cache as read-through from a shared cache service. hotpath should hold a tiny LRU for prefix cache to retain micro-optimizations. we'll measure hit rate and memory footprint in canary.
sophia: tests: add deterministic prompt set (10k short-turn) as regression suite. gate rollout on quality delta < 0.3% and no increased hallucination patterns. integrate with existing eval infra.
ryan: also add rollback triggers: >2% error rate increase, >10ms p99 regression, or >5% cost increase for those routes.
maria: implementation timeline: spike (2w) to prototype C++ service + sidecar shim, perf benchmarks, then 3-week dev cycle for feature flag + telemetry. canary 1 week -> ramping plan.
kevin: dependency list? infra, SRE for canary, obs team for dashboards, security review for new service creds.
maria: noted. will open an RFC doc with the proto, perf numbers from spike, and a checklist for obs + security. @sophia @ryan can you own the metrics & rollout runbook? :thumbsup:
sophia: can do. i'll add dashboards and alert runbook.
ryan: i'll own canary orchestration and rollback automation.
aj: i'll help with sidecar shim and perf tests.
maria: thanks all. i'll post RFC link once it's in doc and drop follow-up thread with spike results.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy job queued for hotpath-spike (not yet started) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
kevin: small nit — ensure we include a client-backoff policy in case hotpath hits resource pressure. otherwise clients will flood router.
maria: good call. adding backpressure + token-bucket.
